rows.claim: spec.md §6.2 (lines 1773, 1793, 1805) says the junction has one output, `out`, wired as "wr_sum/out"

rows.claim: code_map.md:837-842 says every component with one input or one output declares that contract bare, and only a side with two or more ports stays named (apart from Fields's outputs)
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:117 (SumJunction{V,1} u_types is (in1 = V,)) and :193 (Unpack{V,1} y_types is (out1 = V,)); probe:17,19. The docstrings at :25 and :185 state the numbered names.
rows.fix: Add to the code_map.md sentence: 'the one-input `Junction` and the one-output `Unpack` at `N = 1` keep their numbered names `in1` and `out1`, since the arity is a parameter'.
rows.note: Imprecise on a reachable path: a one-wide Junction or Unpack is legal and its ports are named.

rows.claim: `# Design: §11.3, §13.7, D-437.` above Constant, whose comment says 'A constant is never seeded, which is why it carries zero partials'
rows.evidence: spec.md §11.3 (lines 8235-8487) treats root inputs, claims and the frozen roster; rg finds no `Constant`, seeding or pin of a library source in it. The pin is treated in §13.7 (spec.md:12288) and D-312 / D-411 (log.md:14072, 16907).
rows.fix: Replace §11.3 with §9.4 or drop it, keeping §13.7, D-312, D-411.
rows.note: The docstring sentence 'A source set from outside is a root input' links to the glossary, so §11.3 is at most a weak fit for that one sentence.

rows.claim: Comment cites '§7.1's "few KB comfortable"' for the element count past which an array keyword's SArray compiles slowly
rows.evidence: spec.md §7.1 (2184-2267) has no size ceiling. 'a few KB comfortable and tens of KB defensible' is at spec.md:2931, under §8.2 'Workspace idioms'. companions/library_inventory.md:142 repeats the §7.1 cite.
rows.fix: Cite §8.2 for the ceiling at library.jl:459, library.jl:468 and library_inventory.md:142.

rows.claim: The user-visible `@warn` text ends '(§7.1)' for the SArray compile-time claim
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:468; probe:65 prints the warning with '(§7.1)'. The ceiling lives in §8.2 (spec.md:2931), not §7.1.
rows.note: Same defect as the comment at :459; the message reaches users, so it is listed apart.

rows.claim: companions/library_inventory.md:330 lists `Delay(; K, v0)` with 'one output'
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:539 (keyword `taps::Bool = false`), :546-548 (taps = true gives outputs (y, taps)); probe:35; the same companion documents the taps form at lines 432-439.
rows.fix: Row 330: '`Delay(; K, v0, taps = false)` ... `K` ticks of the component's own period (§6.3), the one output `y`, or `(y, taps)` with `taps = true`, `K = 1` the `UnitDelay` in keyword spelling'.
rows.note: Row 330 predates increment 89 (line 432 records the shipping).

rows.claim: `# Design: §11.3, D-312, D-437.` above Source, whose comment says the output depends on neither state nor an input that follows the scalar, hence zero partials
rows.evidence: §11.3 (spec.md:8235-8487) does not treat library sources or the pin; the rule is D-312 / D-411 (log.md:14072, 16907) and §13.7 (spec.md:12288). Tests cite §9.5 for the same refusal (test_library.jl:1096).
rows.fix: Replace §11.3 with §9.5 (conformance) and keep D-312, adding D-411.

rows.claim: code_map.md:759-849 names the helpers of the reset form (`reset_ports`, `signal`, `reset_guard`) but not `reset_handler`
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:964 defines `reset_handler(c::Integrator, _)`, used at :965 as the reset event's handler; rg finds no `reset_handler` in design/code_map.md.
rows.fix: Add `reset_handler` to the Integrator bullet: 'over the helpers `reset_ports`, `signal`, ..., and the event's handler `reset_handler` and guard `reset_guard`'.

rows.claim: code_map.md lists the linear systems' helpers as `static_system`, `realize`, `coefficients_from_roots`, `transfer_coefficients` and the accessors, and omits the port helpers
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:1041-1045 define `port_type`, `as_vector`, `as_port`, which every stage of both abstract parents reads (:1048-1056, :1329-1337); rg finds none in design/code_map.md.
rows.fix: Add to the `AbstractLinearSystem` bullet: 'its stages read the ports through `port_type`, `as_vector` and `as_port`, a width of one being a `Float64`'.

rows.claim: companions/library_inventory.md:440-443 says a root set is refused when 'a product whose imaginary part is not zero to rounding' results, which conjugate pairs pass
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:1172-1189 pairs each complex root with its conjugate by a tolerance relative to the root before the expansion, and the comment above it says the earlier check on expanded coefficients misread rounding (ten-pair sets refused); probe:82-83.
rows.fix: Zero-Pole bullet: 'Roots real or complex; each complex root must have a conjugate partner within `1e-12` relative to the root, which the pairing pass checks before the expansion, and the real coefficients then meet the existing refusals.'
rows.note: The code comment records the move. No log entry was searched for.

rows.claim: The TransferFunction and DiscreteTransferFunction docstrings (:1241, :1445) state the refusals of the root spelling as mixing the spellings, roots not closed under conjugation and more zeros than poles
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:1198-1206 also refuses (as ArgumentError) a call with neither spelling complete (`num` without `den`, nothing given), `zeros` or `gain` without `poles`, and a non-real `gain`; probe:77,79,80,81,84. Test:1921 pins the 'without `poles`' one.
rows.fix: After 'and more zeros than poles' add: 'so is a call that gives neither spelling whole, `zeros` or `gain` without `poles`, and a `gain` that is not real.'
rows.note: The retained ArgumentError is the same kind, so the gap is in the listed cases only.

rows.claim: code_map.md:845-846 says nothing in the package depends on library.jl, so src/Redstone.jl includes it last
rows.evidence: src/Redstone.jl:35-36 includes library.jl and then precompile.jl, and src/precompile.jl:19-21 calls `Library.Step`, `Library.DiscretePID`, `Library.FirstOrderLag`; code_map.md:1032 says precompile.jl is included 'after the library it uses'.
rows.fix: 'Nothing in the package but the precompile workload depends on it, so `src/Redstone.jl` includes it after the core and before `precompile.jl`.'
rows.note: Two code_map entries disagree on the order.

Unpack{V,N}: input u an SVector{N,V}, outputs out1..outN typed V, outi = u[i], stateless
Fields{V}: outputs take the field names and types of V, one level, and any other V (Float64, SArray, Tuple, abstract, empty) is refused as ArgumentError
Switch{V}: inputs in1, in2 typed V and select Bool, y = in1 while select holds; AlgebraicCycle on a memoryless select loop
Select{V,K}: one input per instance of K named after it plus select::K, output y typed V; abstract K or an instance named select is ArgumentError
Constant(value): no inputs, no state, y pinned at V, published from stage 1
UnitDelay(s0): y = s from stage 1, s0 first, s+ = u, one type V
Freeze{V}: output u with partials dropped, pinned at V; V other than Float64 or an SArray of Float64 is a TypeError
StopRequest(; reason = ""): Bool input u, StopFlag output y (STOP_REQUESTED while u holds), stop_reason reports reason
code_map: as_static makes the SArray of its size of an array keyword of any kind and warns once past STATIC_WARN_LENGTH
Inventory: two array lengths are Julia's DimensionMismatch
Delay(; K, v0, taps): K >= 1 else ArgumentError, v0 broadcast to V, taps adds output taps newest first with taps[K] = y
DiscreteIntegrator: s+ = s + Dt u, y = s stage 1, reset form adds Bool input and writes s0 at the level
DiscreteLimitedIntegrator: outputs (out, saturation::Int8 code 1/-1/0), clamp update, lower not below upper is ArgumentError
RateLimiter(; rising, falling = rising, s0): y = s + clamp(u - s, -falling Dt, rising Dt), non-positive rates ArgumentError
Backlash(; width, s0): y = clamp(s, u - w/2, u + w/2), non-positive width ArgumentError
GaussianWhiteNoise: exactly one of sigma and psd (ArgumentError otherwise), sigma^2 = Q/Dt, store k reads N+1 after N ticks past t0
Source{V}(f), Source(f) = Source{Float64}(f): y = f(t) pinned at V, f gets Float64 time, wrong type refused as ConformanceFailure then StepError later
Integrator(; x0, reset): x-dot = u, reset adds Bool input, one non-localized state event reset
FirstOrderLag(; tau, x0): x-dot = (u - x)/tau, tau not positive in every component is ArgumentError, scalar case equals TransferFunction(num=(1,), den=(tau,1), u0=x0)
AbstractLinearSystem{FT}: FT false when D is zero (stage 1), true otherwise (stage 2), ports u and y
StateSpace keywords A,B,C,D,x0: SVector state, scalar or SVector ports, ArgumentError for misfit shapes, wrong x0 length, empty A
realize(num, den): controllable canonical form (; A,B,C,D) as SMatrix of Float64, monic, direct term split
TransferFunction: starts at rest or at the steady state G(0) u0, four refusals, feedthrough class by degree
AbstractDiscreteLinearSystem{FT}: stages over held and realization(c, Dt), s_init from initial_state
DiscreteStateSpace: keywords as StateSpace with s0 for x0, x0 not accepted
DiscreteTransferFunction: steady state G(1) u0, pole at z = 1 refused within 1e-12 of the magnitude sum, (1,-0.7,-0.3) refused
DiscretizedStateSpace(continuous) and keyword form both accepted, keywords as StateSpace
